newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 12.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Korea Employers' Federation vice president Cho Nam-hong asked business groups to freeze worker wages this year.
- Choi Hyung-woo, a leading New Korea Party member was hospitalised yesterday. This is expected to have an influence over December presidential election.

- President Kim Young-sam has decided on Lee Han-dong as the next New Korea Party chairman, a senior party official said. Lee is a leading member of the ruling New Korea Party. President Kim is expected to announce the appointment tomorrow.
- The New Korea Party Chairman Lee Hong-koo, virtually threw his hat in the ring for the party's presidential candidacy yesterday.
- The opposition parties yesterday renewed their call for President Kim Young-sam's son Hyon-Chol's presence at a special National Assembly committee investigating the Hanbo loan scandal.
- The United States stepped up its trade pressure on Seoul, raising concerns over South Korea's ongoing frugality campaign and efforts to constrain the widening current account deficit.
